name: agents-system
description: npm-shipped default plugins for agents-cli — the lightweight, no-paid-key workflows that ship with the system layer. Heavier or key-gated plugins live in .agents-extras instead.

plugins.name: code
plugins.description: Coding-workflow plugin for the manager/router engineering loop. `/code:loop` drains a queue end-to-end (single ticket or many: plan, code, test, review, rebase, fix CI, merge), `/code:verify` runs the end-to-end gate (canonical test per changed surface, read from the project's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md), `/code:review` reviews every PR opened in parallel — plus a security pass on risk-touching diffs — and merges per verdict, `/code:ship` is the post-merge gate for distributables (publish, confirm live on the public channel, activate where it runs, verify the real surface), `/code:quality` runs a read-only code-health diagnostic and opens an HTML report, `/code:learn` reflects on a session and routes durable lessons to the right skill/rule/memory without overfitting, `/commit` splits the working tree into the maximum number of small logical commits.

plugins.name: work
plugins.description: work — get a project's work done across the fleet, any kind, not just code. `/work:dispatch` takes ONE unit of work (a ticket, a described task, or 'the next thing on <project>'), finds/pulls the ticket while deduping against in-flight PRs and live sessions, classifies it as coding vs non-coding, files it clean if missing, then self-refers to the plugin that owns the execution — the `code` plugin for engineering, or `social`/`design`/`share` plus the `browser` skill and `secrets` for non-coding work (outreach, research, a design asset, a real web/portal task). Single-target dispatch, not a board sweep — deciding the whole board (keep/cancel/reprioritize) and surfacing calls that need the human is `/triage`'s job. The kind-agnostic superset of `/dispatch`.

plugins.name: design
plugins.description: design — a keyless, offline-first design front door. `/design` routes a design intent to a mode and renders it as self-contained HTML/SVG (no CDN, no paid keys): UI screens and flows (interface), clickable prototypes (prototype), design systems and tokens (system), architecture/flow/ER diagrams (diagram, via plan-render's diagram-conventions), infographics and data-stories (dataviz), slide decks (deck), and critique of an existing screen (critique). Vector assets (OG cards, SVG logos, icon sets, posters) render offline too; true raster (photo, illustration, painterly cover) is an optional layer that degrades to a spec plus an editable placeholder plus enable-steps rather than hard-failing. Every mode loads design-core first: visual hierarchy, WCAG AA contrast, colorblind-safe palettes, brand-probe, precise non-marketing copy, and render/screenshot/critique verification. Brand plugins layer on top by calling /design; brand is optional, never required.

plugins.name: fleet
plugins.description: fleet — fleet-wide operations across every machine registered with `agents devices`. `/fleet:sync` pulls every registered DotAgent repo (system, user, and extras) to origin latest on every online device, then refreshes the installed agents — non-destructive (git merge --ff-only only; reports repos blocked by local edits instead of clobbering), handling the fast-forward workaround, the transient GitHub-SSH throttle, and Windows PowerShell quoting, ending with a repo x device matrix. `/fleet:onboard <device>` brings a bare new device up to fleet parity (agents-cli, agent CLIs, DotAgent repos, shared SSH key, PATH shim, device registration, agent auth) — discovery-first, additive, idempotent, credentials via sanctioned paths only, never copied host-to-host.

plugins.name: git
plugins.description: git — pure git plumbing commands that aren't tied to code logic. `/git:prune` removes merged branches and worktrees with hard data-loss guards (skips anything with uncommitted changes, stashes, unmerged commits, locks, or detached HEAD), using `git rev-list --count origin/$MAIN..HEAD == 0` as the load-bearing 'nothing to lose' check. `/git:tag-release` creates and pushes an annotated release tag (never force, never re-points an existing tag). The code-aware loop (`/commit`, `/review`, `/code:loop`) lives in the `code` plugin.

plugins.name: share
plugins.description: share — publish an HTML artifact (a plan, viz, or report) to a shareable link on your own Cloudflare R2 (zero egress, ~$0) via `agents share`. `/share:public` posts a public link with an auto-generated OG cover (a screenshot of the page's hero) so it unfurls into a preview card in Slack/iMessage/Twitter/Discord; `/share:private` posts an unlisted, auto-expiring link with no preview card (unguessable but still public-read — not authenticated). Requires a one-time `agents share setup` (provisions an R2 bucket + Worker) or `agents share join`.

plugins.name: social
plugins.description: social — turn a content agent's post archive into strategy. social:audit (parse+dedup+cluster+12x3 taxonomy), social:align (audience/ICP fit: buyer vs amplifier, gaps + re-weighting), social:schedule (coverage-deduped engagement-rubric backlog scheduled to X/LinkedIn via getlate). Built from a real ~4,600-draft audit.

plugins.name: swarm
plugins.description: swarm — fan a task out across a team of parallel coding agents via `agents teams` (the modern replacement for the deprecated Swarmify MCP). `/swarm:run` is the generic fan-out — decompose an arbitrary goal into independent tracks, spawn a mixed team, monitor, and synthesize (the catch-all for work that doesn't fit the specialized modes); `/swarm:plan` researches hard and drafts an OpenSpec-grade change proposal, then has independent agents plan it blind and reconciles; `/swarm:spec` reverse-engineers the OpenSpec source-of-truth spec (requirements + Given/When/Then scenarios) from the real code, then has independent agents spec it blind and drift-checks every requirement against actual behavior; `/swarm:debug` traces the data path and confirms the root cause with blind, different-provider verifiers (scaled to the bug) before any fix; `/swarm:test` splits a scope into areas and covers each in parallel; `/swarm:qa` maps an app's QA surface, provisions instances on multiple ports, and fans QA agents across them in waves via `agents browser`, then ranks a ship/no-ship verdict. Each command invokes its same-named skill; the shared `agents teams` engine (provider discovery, boundary contracts, judgment-based sizing) lives in the internal `swarm:orchestrate` skill.
